entry.title: When Are We Near Nash? Certifying Solutions in General-Sum Games
entry.summary:
Heuristic solvers for general-sum extensive-form games produce a stream of iterates, and practice reports the NashGap of the returned profile. We ask what a solver can know about its own iterates from the regret accumulators and the terminal-distribution accumulators its updates already maintain. In two-player games the NashGap of a weighted average strategy equals, at the maximizing player, the weighted external regret plus a signed value correction.

Source: arXiv Game Theory, Complex Systems & Soc-Phys (cs.GT, nlin.AO, physics.soc-ph) · Tags: #decision-theory #complex-systems #ml-theory #agents

entry.title: Computing the Nucleon of Matching Games
entry.summary:
The nucleon is the multiplicative counterpart of the nucleolus: it lexicographically maximizes the fraction of its stand-alone value that each coalition receives. We study exact nucleon computation in matching games and in two extensions: $b$-matching games, in which players may have several partners, and partitioned matching games, in which one player may own several vertices. We resolve three open problems from a recent survey.

Source: arXiv Game Theory, Complex Systems & Soc-Phys (cs.GT, nlin.AO, physics.soc-ph) · Tags: #decision-theory #complex-systems #combinatorics

entry.title: Condensation and optimal targeting of repeated forcing in heterogeneous networks
entry.summary:
Many networks receive repeated external forcing through a subset of entry nodes, for example infections imported from another population, information seeded by a campaign, or invasive species arriving through ports. We study how concentrating such forcing on important entry nodes, with seeding probability $π_i\propto w_i^γ$, changes the size of the resulting cascades in a stochastic SIR model on bipartite networks. The response to one seeding event is linear in the degree of the seeded node, so the relative gain from targeting does not depend on transmissibility.

Source: arXiv Game Theory, Complex Systems & Soc-Phys (cs.GT, nlin.AO, physics.soc-ph) · Tags: #decision-theory #complex-systems

entry.title: Energy-fed commitment: a minimal model of random selection followed by reinforcement
entry.summary:
When a symmetric instability is crossed, fluctuations choose one of several equivalent branches. We study a minimal stochastic model of what can then make that choice progressively harder to undo. After selection, the stiffness of the selected state grows in proportion to the energy released each time the structure recovers from a perturbation; in this conservative model that energy equals, up to small and explicitly computed terms, the work absorbed from the perturbing agent.

Source: arXiv Game Theory, Complex Systems & Soc-Phys (cs.GT, nlin.AO, physics.soc-ph) · Tags: #decision-theory #complex-systems #agents

entry.title: Formalizing Cooperation and Competition: An AI-Assisted Mathematical Addendum to a 2018 Planning Thesis
entry.summary:
We present an AI-assisted mathematical addendum to Strategic Trip Planning: Striking a Balance Between Competition and Cooperation (Amar, 2018). We reconstruct selected relationships between strategic choice, cooperative stability, participant approval and enforcement. The thesis's Nash-to-core proposition is under-specified until outsider opportunities are stated.

Source: arXiv Game Theory, Complex Systems & Soc-Phys (cs.GT, nlin.AO, physics.soc-ph) · Tags: #decision-theory #complex-systems #ml-theory

entry.title: Urban climate regressions require representative monitoring networks
entry.summary:
Land use regression models relate intra-urban air temperature to spatial predictors such as building volume, tree canopy cover and topography, and are increasingly used to produce fine-scale temperature maps. However, the accuracy of these estimates can be compromised by unrepresentative monitoring networks. Here we show that reference weather station networks, designed for regional rather than intra-urban monitoring, sample only a narrow portion of a city's spatial heterogeneity, missing both the densely built core and the cool, vegetated periphery that set the two ends of the urban temperature range.

Source: arXiv Game Theory, Complex Systems & Soc-Phys (cs.GT, nlin.AO, physics.soc-ph) · Tags: #decision-theory #complex-systems #climate-earth #combinatorics

entry.title: GSP Autobidding Equilibria with Few Advertisers or Slots
entry.summary:
In sponsored-shopping auctions, one advertiser may win several positions, and a product that is never displayed may determine the prices of several winners. Under generalized second-price (GSP) pricing without self-pricing, these interactions couple allocation and payment through a single global ranking. We prove that exact autobidding equilibria under budget and return-on-investment (ROI) constraints can be computed in polynomial time whenever either the number $n$ of advertisers or the number $K$ of display slots is fixed.

Source: arXiv Game Theory, Complex Systems & Soc-Phys (cs.GT, nlin.AO, physics.soc-ph) · Tags: #decision-theory #complex-systems

entry.title: Noise-driven loss of chimera states and bifurcations in a nonlocal oscillator ring
entry.summary:
Independent phase noise can remove the spatial contrast of a chimera while leaving substantial collective coherence. We study this transition in a nonlocally coupled Kuramoto--Sakaguchi ring with a cosine kernel using the nonlinear Fokker--Planck equation. Stationary self-consistency and spatial spectra identify two bifurcations of the uniform ordered state at a reference phase lag.

Source: arXiv Game Theory, Complex Systems & Soc-Phys (cs.GT, nlin.AO, physics.soc-ph) · Tags: #decision-theory #complex-systems

entry.title: Pareto Inefficiency of EFX
entry.summary:
We consider the problem of allocating indivisible goods to agents with additive valuations, under two classic notions of fairness and efficiency: envy-freeness up to any good (EFX) and Pareto optimality. While some of the earliest work on EFX showed that Pareto optimal EFX allocations may not exist if agents can have zero value for some goods, it has remained open whether the same is true when all values are positive. We present a simple instance in which every good has positive value to every agent, but no Pareto optimal EFX allocation exists.

Source: arXiv Game Theory, Complex Systems & Soc-Phys (cs.GT, nlin.AO, physics.soc-ph) · Tags: #decision-theory #complex-systems #agents
